---
title: "Section 1: From Twenty Movies to an Unknown Proportion"
---

Let $p$ represent the unknown proportion of movies in the relevant population that pass the Bechdel test.

$p = P$(a randomly selected movie passes the Bechdel test)

If $p = 0.30$, then approximately 30% of movies in the population pass.

If $p = 0.50$, then approximately half pass.

If $p = 0.80$, then approximately 80% pass.

We do not know the true value of $p$. What we observe is the sample proportion:

$\hat{p} = y/n$

Here:

$\hat{p} = 9/20 = 0.45$

The sample tells us that 45% of these 20 movies passed. However, $\hat{p}$ and $p$ are not the same thing. $p$ is the unknown population proportion we want to estimate and $\hat{p}$ is a statistic calculated from the particular sample we observed.
